{
  "hook": "Ramnista vineyard sits at 350-450 meters on Mount Vermio's northeast slopes, where schist-limestone soils and cold nights build Xinomavro's structure. Kir Yianni sources from 40-year-old vines here, yielding a Naoussa red with redcurrant snap and olive savor. Awards pile up across vintages, from TEXSOM golds in 2012 and 2015 to bronzes in 2017.",
  "wine_summary": "Kir Yianni, founded by Yiannis Boutaris in 1997, shifted from family roots at Kir-Yianni to modern Naoussa focus, emphasizing single-vineyard sites like Ramnista. This 100% Xinomavro adheres to Naoussa PDO rules requiring full Xinomavro for reds, delivering ageworthy depth that rivals Piedmont Nebbiolo at lower prices. The producer's push for terroir transparency puts Ramnista on U.S. lists seeking Greek alternatives to Barolo.",
  "terroir_expression": "Naoussa's clay-limestone and schist soils on Mount Vermio's slopes retain water for Xinomavro's steady ripening amid continental summers and harsh winters. Elevations up to 450 meters create diurnal swings that lock in acidity, translating to vibrant red fruit and mineral edge in the glass. Schist adds smoky spice, while calcareous marls contribute firm tannins that evolve into leather over time.",
  "vinification_summary": "Kir Yianni destems and crushes Xinomavro gently, fermenting in temperature-controlled stainless tanks to preserve fruit purity before malolactic fermentation softens acidity. The wine then ages 12 months in French oak barriques (one-third new), integrating wood spice without overwhelming site character—oak here amplifies Ramnista's earth notes rather than dominating.",
  "food_pairing": "Lamb souvlaki with yogurt-tzatziki cuts through the wine's tannins while acidity matches charred meat juices. Pasta alla Norma (eggplant-tomato sauce) finds balance in Xinomavro's herbal lift against sweet veg and salty ricotta salata. Roast leg of lamb with rosemary handles structure via fat and herb synergy. Nashville hot chicken relies on high acidity to tame spice and refresh palate between bites. Osso buco Milanese pairs fine dining richness with the wine's savory olive and slow-braised marrow.",
  "comparable_wines": "Thymiopoulos Naoussa Earth & Sky — shared Xinomavro structure from schist soils, but earthier with less oak. Vietti Barolo Castiglione — Nebbiolo parallel in tannin grip and cherry core, though Naoussa edges on value. Kir Yianni Naoussa Paragogi — same producer's entry-level, softer tannins from younger vines.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-plus bodied Xinomavro with firm tannins and savory tomato leaf persistence",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2015 and older now through 2028; store in cool darkness at 55°F to let tannins integrate. Younger 2017 needs 2 more years for fruit polish.",
  "value_assessment": "$25-35 retail positions Ramnista against Alpha Estate Xinomavro ($28) or entry Barbaresco ($35). Consistent TEXSOM medals across vintages justify the spend for structured Greek red. Skip pricier Piedmont imports—same aging arc at half cost.",
  "market_position": "Sommeliers stock it on Greek or 'next Nebbiolo' lists at mid-tier restaurants like NYC's Pylos. Retail hits wine bars and shops targeting collectors exploring Macedonia. Casual adventurers grab it via importers like Skurnik for home trials.",
  "insider_take": "Buy Ramnista over softer Naoussa blends if you want true Xinomavro backbone that builds cellars. Most overlook the schist-driven spice, chasing fruitier versions that fade early. Skip if light Pinots are your limit—this demands food and patience.",

parsed.hook: Ramnista vineyard sits at 350-450 meters on Mount Vermio's northeast slopes, where schist-limestone soils and cold nights build Xinomavro's structure. Kir Yianni sources from 40-year-old vines here, yielding a Naoussa red with redcurrant snap and olive savor. Awards pile up across vintages, from TEXSOM golds in 2012 and 2015 to bronzes in 2017.
parsed.wine_summary: Kir Yianni, founded by Yiannis Boutaris in 1997, shifted from family roots at Kir-Yianni to modern Naoussa focus, emphasizing single-vineyard sites like Ramnista. This 100% Xinomavro adheres to Naoussa PDO rules requiring full Xinomavro for reds, delivering ageworthy depth that rivals Piedmont Nebbiolo at lower prices. The producer's push for terroir transparency puts Ramnista on U.S. lists seeking Greek alternatives to Barolo.
parsed.terroir_expression: Naoussa's clay-limestone and schist soils on Mount Vermio's slopes retain water for Xinomavro's steady ripening amid continental summers and harsh winters. Elevations up to 450 meters create diurnal swings that lock in acidity, translating to vibrant red fruit and mineral edge in the glass. Schist adds smoky spice, while calcareous marls contribute firm tannins that evolve into leather over time.
parsed.vinification_summary: Kir Yianni destems and crushes Xinomavro gently, fermenting in temperature-controlled stainless tanks to preserve fruit purity before malolactic fermentation softens acidity. The wine then ages 12 months in French oak barriques (one-third new), integrating wood spice without overwhelming site character—oak here amplifies Ramnista's earth notes rather than dominating.
parsed.food_pairing: Lamb souvlaki with yogurt-tzatziki cuts through the wine's tannins while acidity matches charred meat juices. Pasta alla Norma (eggplant-tomato sauce) finds balance in Xinomavro's herbal lift against sweet veg and salty ricotta salata. Roast leg of lamb with rosemary handles structure via fat and herb synergy. Nashville hot chicken relies on high acidity to tame spice and refresh palate between bites. Osso buco Milanese pairs fine dining richness with the wine's savory olive and slow-braised marrow.
parsed.comparable_wines: Thymiopoulos Naoussa Earth & Sky — shared Xinomavro structure from schist soils, but earthier with less oak. Vietti Barolo Castiglione — Nebbiolo parallel in tannin grip and cherry core, though Naoussa edges on value. Kir Yianni Naoussa Paragogi — same producer's entry-level, softer tannins from younger vines.
parsed.style_profile: Medium-plus bodied Xinomavro with firm tannins and savory tomato leaf persistence
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink 2015 and older now through 2028; store in cool darkness at 55°F to let tannins integrate. Younger 2017 needs 2 more years for fruit polish.
parsed.value_assessment: $25-35 retail positions Ramnista against Alpha Estate Xinomavro ($28) or entry Barbaresco ($35). Consistent TEXSOM medals across vintages justify the spend for structured Greek red. Skip pricier Piedmont imports—same aging arc at half cost.
parsed.market_position: Sommeliers stock it on Greek or 'next Nebbiolo' lists at mid-tier restaurants like NYC's Pylos. Retail hits wine bars and shops targeting collectors exploring Macedonia. Casual adventurers grab it via importers like Skurnik for home trials.
parsed.insider_take: Buy Ramnista over softer Naoussa blends if you want true Xinomavro backbone that builds cellars. Most overlook the schist-driven spice, chasing fruitier versions that fade early. Skip if light Pinots are your limit—this demands food and patience.
